name: Dedua
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Ceder, Sune (& Britt Ceder) 1990. Dedua grammar essentials. SIL PNG ms, 204 pp. (per Glottolog dedu1240 refs); also Pilhofer 1928-29 Formenlehre von zehn Mundarten des Kate.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1970. The Selepet language within the Finisterre-Huon phylum (New Guinea). PhD thesis, Australian National University. xi + 477 leaves.
sources.note: The only stress statements are for Selepet (Western Huon), e.g. ch. 5 'Stress group (word): A stress group contains one primary stress occurring on the initial syllable followed by secondary stresses occurring on subsequent alternate syllables' and 'Since stress is predictable it is left unmarked'. Chapter 10 (typology of Finisterre-Huon languages) has no remarks on stress; Dedua (as 'Depe [Dedua]') occurs only in the history-of-research survey (ch. 1). Not a Dedua stress source.

sources.citation: Wikipedia. Dedua language (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dedua_language), raw wikitext fetched sources 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Phonology section gives the consonant and vowel inventory only (sourced to the SIL OPD linked as external link); no mention of stress. Names two dialects, Dzeigoc and Fanic.

sources.citation: SIL PNG Branch. 2004. Organised Phonology Data: Dedua Language [DED], Finschhafen – Morobe Province. Data checked by Sune and Britt Ceder (2003). 5 pp. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG. (Bibliography line: Ceder, Sune, and Britt Ceder. 1990. Manuscripts. SIL, Ukarumpa.)
sources.note: Nothing. The OPD has inventory, consonant/vowel contrast lists, syllable patterns (V, VV, VC, CV, CVV, CVC, CVVC), phonological and orthographic conventions, a transcribed text and a one-line bibliography; there is no stress/suprasegmental section and the phonemic transcription of the recorded passage (p. 4, checked on the rendered page image) carries no stress marks. sil.org itself is behind a Cloudflare challenge; the file was taken from the Wayback Machine snapshot 20240910131257 of the SIL URL linked from Wikipedia.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1973. Towards a typology of the Finisterre-Huon languages, New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-22. Canberra: ANU. viii + 80 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-B22.
sources.harvard_location: DIV Offsite Storage - Ask at Circulation (Pamph. folio) BS 354.Z91
sources.note: Nothing about stress. Section 1 Phonology (pp. 5-6: 1.1 Phonemes, 1.2 Syllable structure, 1.3 Morphophonemics) compares ten representative languages (Kâte, Ono, Selepet, Kube, Nabak, Uri, Wantoat, Kewieng, Rawa, Kovai) on phoneme inventories, syllable shapes and vowel length; Dedua appears only in the language list (Eastern Huon Family, a. Dedua, p. vii) and is not one of the ten compared languages.
